selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What central belief is affirmed in the passage?
questions.answer: The passage affirms that only Allah is truly worthy of worship and that He exists necessarily as the One God.

questions.question: Whose united testimony is presented as evidence in this passage?
questions.answer: The united testimony of all the prophets is presented as the evidence.

questions.question: What gives force to the prophets’ shared testimony?
questions.answer: Their clear and extraordinary miracles give strength to their testimony.

questions.question: How do the miracles function in relation to the prophets’ message?
questions.answer: They confirm the prophets’ mission and support the truth of what they proclaim.

questions.question: What does the passage show about the prophets as a group?
questions.answer: It shows that they are in agreement on Allah’s existence and on His oneness.

questions.question: Why is their agreement important for understanding the claim being made?
questions.answer: Because a unanimous message from all prophets carries strong weight and points to a single divine truth.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the relationship between miracle and belief?
questions.answer: It suggests that miracles are signs from Allah that strengthen and validate belief.

questions.question: Which two major ideas about Allah are especially highlighted here?
questions.answer: His necessary existence and His unity are especially highlighted.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that all prophets are described as unanimous?
questions.answer: It can be inferred that their message is consistent, not confused or contradictory, and comes from the same source.

questions.question: In one sentence, what is the main point of the passage?
questions.answer: The main point is that the unanimous witness of all prophets, supported by their miracles, is a powerful proof of Allah’s necessary existence and oneness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what statement stands at the beginning of the message?
questions.answer: It begins with the declaration that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What kind of evidence is emphasized instead of philosophical argument alone?
questions.answer: The passage emphasizes prophetic agreement backed by miracles.

questions.question: Who are the witnesses in this passage: scholars, saints, angels, or prophets?
questions.answer: The witnesses in this passage are the prophets.

questions.question: What quality of the prophets’ witness makes it especially compelling?
questions.answer: Its complete unity makes it especially compelling.

questions.question: How are the miracles described in relation to brightness or clarity?
questions.answer: They are described as radiant and striking signs.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by connecting Allah’s existence with unity?
questions.answer: It means Allah exists necessarily and is not one among many, but the One without partner.

questions.question: How does the passage connect signs and truth?
questions.answer: It presents miracles as signs that verify the truth of the prophets’ message.

questions.question: What kind of conclusion is the reader being led to accept?
questions.answer: The reader is being led to accept that Allah alone is the necessary and unique God.

questions.question: What may be inferred about disagreement among prophets on this issue?
questions.answer: The passage implies there is no disagreement among them on this issue.

questions.question: Why would this passage strengthen a believer’s faith?
questions.answer: It strengthens faith by showing that all prophets delivered the same core truth and that their miracles supported it.

questions.question: What theological truth does the passage aim to prove?
questions.answer: It aims to prove Allah’s necessary existence and oneness.

questions.question: Through whose consensus is this truth shown?
questions.answer: It is shown through the consensus of all the prophets.

questions.question: What role do miracles play in this proof?
questions.answer: They serve as confirming signs that support the prophets and what they brought.

questions.question: Does the passage present the prophets as isolated individuals or as a united body of witnesses?
questions.answer: It presents them as a united body of witnesses.
